newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: TECHNOLOGY TO CURB GROWING BUREAUCRACY IN BOTSWANA.
newsitem.headline: TECHNOLOGY TO CURB GROWING BUREAUCRACY IN BOTSWANA.

text.p: Botswana is to curtail the growth of its civil service and further its development aims with increasing use of information technology, according to a senior government minister.

"We have to explore ways of increasing productivity in the civil service rather than continue to increase manpower in government departments," Vice President and Minister for Finance and Development Planning, Festus Mogae, said late on Thursday.
Mogae said for the country's National Development Plan 8 (NDP8), to run from 1997 to 2002, the information technology budget would be three times the spending during NDP7.
Botswana budgeted 26 million pula for the development of government computer services during NDP7. No outturn figures are available.

Mogae was speaking at the opening of an information technology training centre in the capital Gaborone -- the first venture into mainland Africa by the India-based National Institute for Information Technology.
